theme: String instruments normally played by drawing a bow across them.
decoy: Traditional and orchestral string instruments with a neck

members.title: Violin
members.description: Four-string instrument tuned in fifths and held under the chin.

members.title: Cello
members.description: Large four-string instrument held between the knees, resting on an endpin.

members.title: Erhu
members.description: Chinese two-string instrument with a small snakeskin-covered sound box.

members.title: Rebec
members.description: Medieval pear-shaped instrument with three strings, carved from one piece of wood.

members.title: Morin khuur
members.description: Mongolian two-string instrument whose pegbox is carved as a horse's head.

members.title: Gusle
members.description: Balkan single-string instrument that accompanies recited epic poetry.

members.title: Haegeum
members.description: Korean two-string instrument with a small round sound box.

members.title: Kemenche
members.description: Small bottle-shaped Black Sea instrument with three strings, held upright on the knee.

intruders.title: Mandolin
intruders.description: Eight-string instrument in paired courses, tuned G-D-A-E like a violin.
intruders.why: Plucked with a plectrum, not bowed; its strings share the violin's tuning, which makes it look like a relative.

intruders.title: Hurdy-gurdy
intruders.description: Medieval instrument with melody and drone strings, played on the lap.
intruders.why: Its strings are sounded by a crank-turned rosined wheel, not a bow, though it has a fiddle-like body and sustained tone.

theme: Italian tempo markings: terms that tell the performer how fast the music should go.
decoy: Italian performance directions written in scores

members.title: Largo
members.description: Italian for 'broad'; stately and very drawn out.

members.title: Adagio
members.description: Italian for 'at ease'; the usual marking for slow movements.

members.title: Andante
members.description: Italian for 'walking'; an easy, flowing pace.

members.title: Allegro
members.description: Italian for 'cheerful'; brisk, the usual choice for opening movements.

members.title: Presto
members.description: Italian for 'quickly'; very rapid, often used in finales.

members.title: Lento
members.description: Italian for 'sluggish'; unhurried and slow.

members.title: Grave
members.description: Italian for 'heavy'; solemn and extremely slow.

members.title: Moderato
members.description: Italian for 'restrained'; neither hurried nor dragging.

members.title: Vivace
members.description: Italian for 'lively'; quick and spirited.

intruders.title: Forte
intruders.description: Italian for 'strong'; abbreviated as a single letter f.
intruders.why: A dynamic marking for loudness, not a rate of pulse; it appears in the same Italian vocabulary on the same scores.

intruders.title: Legato
intruders.description: Italian for 'tied'; notes joined smoothly without gaps.
intruders.why: An articulation marking about how notes connect, not how fast they go; it sits alongside tempo words in scores.

theme: Pitched percussion whose sounding parts are all metal.
decoy: Pitched percussion instruments played by striking

members.title: Vibraphone
members.description: Bar instrument with motor-driven discs in its resonators that add a pulsing tremolo.

members.title: Tubular bells
members.description: Hanging row of long tubes struck at the top with rawhide hammers.

members.title: Crotales
members.description: Small thick tuned discs, played with mallets or bowed.

members.title: Handbells
members.description: Individually held tuned bells rung in teams, each player covering a few notes.

members.title: Saron
members.description: Javanese gamelan instrument of thick bars resting over a trough.

members.title: Hang
members.description: Swiss-made lens-shaped instrument with dimpled note fields, played with the hands.

members.title: Gender
members.description: Balinese instrument of thin bars suspended over bamboo resonators.

members.title: Carillon
members.description: Tower instrument of at least twenty-three bells played from a baton keyboard.

members.title: Almglocken
members.description: Tuned cowbells without clappers, arranged chromatically and struck with sticks.

intruders.title: Xylophone
intruders.description: Bar instrument with a bright, dry tone, played with hard mallets.
intruders.why: Its bars are wood (rosewood or synthetic), not metal; it is laid out exactly like the vibraphone.

intruders.title: Marimba
intruders.description: Deep-toned bar instrument with long resonator tubes beneath its keyboard.
intruders.why: Its bars are rosewood; only the resonator tubes underneath are metal.

intruders.title: Balafon
intruders.description: West African bar instrument with gourds hung beneath the keys.
intruders.why: Its keys are wooden slats and its resonators are gourds.

theme: Drums whose sound comes from a stretched membrane or head.
decoy: Hand-played and stick-played drums from around the world

members.title: Snare drum
members.description: Shallow cylinder with wires strung across the bottom for a crisp rattle.

members.title: Timpani
members.description: Large copper kettles tuned with pedals, played with felt mallets.

members.title: Bongos
members.description: Pair of small joined Cuban drums held between the knees.

members.title: Djembe
members.description: West African goblet-shaped drum played with bare hands.

members.title: Tabla
members.description: North Indian pair of hand drums with a black tuning paste spot.

members.title: Bodhran
members.description: Irish frame drum played with a double-ended wooden beater.

members.title: Conga
members.description: Tall narrow Afro-Cuban drum, often played in sets of two or three.

members.title: Talking drum
members.description: West African hourglass drum squeezed under the arm to bend its pitch.

members.title: Darbuka
members.description: Goblet drum of the Middle East, played with sharp finger strokes.

intruders.title: Cajon
intruders.description: Peruvian box drum that the player sits on and slaps.
intruders.why: It is a wooden box whose thin plywood front is struck; there is no stretched skin or head.

intruders.title: Steelpan
intruders.description: Trinidadian drum hammered from an oil barrel into tuned note areas.
intruders.why: Called a drum, but it sounds from vibrating hammered steel, not a membrane.

intruders.title: Slit drum
intruders.description: Hollowed log drum with a long slot cut along its top.
intruders.why: The wooden body itself vibrates; nothing is stretched over it.

theme: Operas: dramas written to be staged in an opera house, with singers acting out roles in costume.
decoy: Large-scale works for vocal soloists, chorus, and orchestra

members.title: La traviata
members.description: Verdi's 1853 work about a Parisian courtesan who gives up her lover.

members.title: The Magic Flute
members.description: Mozart's 1791 work with a bird-catcher, a prince, and the Queen of the Night.

members.title: Tosca
members.description: Puccini's 1900 work set in Rome over a single day in 1800.

members.title: Aida
members.description: Verdi's 1871 work about an Ethiopian princess enslaved in Egypt.

members.title: Rigoletto
members.description: Verdi's 1851 work about a hunchbacked jester at the court of Mantua.

members.title: Madama Butterfly
members.description: Puccini's 1904 work about a young geisha in Nagasaki.

members.title: Fidelio
members.description: Beethoven's only work of its kind, about a wife rescuing her imprisoned husband.

members.title: Tristan und Isolde
members.description: Wagner's 1865 work whose opening chord became famous in harmony textbooks.

members.title: Don Giovanni
members.description: Mozart's 1787 work about a seducer dragged down by a statue.

members.title: Eugene Onegin
members.description: Tchaikovsky's 1879 work after Pushkin's novel in verse.

intruders.title: Messiah
intruders.description: Handel's 1742 work in three parts, famous for its Hallelujah chorus.
intruders.why: An oratorio, sung in concert without staging, costumes, or characters acting out a plot.

intruders.title: The Creation
intruders.description: Haydn's 1798 work in three parts, with the archangels as narrators.
intruders.why: An oratorio written for concert performance, not a staged drama.

theme: Genres that originated in the United States.
decoy: Popular and dance music genres that arose in the 20th century

members.title: Jazz
members.description: Improvisation-heavy style that grew in New Orleans around 1900.

members.title: Blues
members.description: Twelve-bar form with bent notes, from the Mississippi Delta and beyond.

members.title: Bluegrass
members.description: Fast acoustic string-band music with banjo rolls and high harmony.

members.title: Hip hop
members.description: Rapping over breakbeats, first heard at Bronx block parties.

members.title: Ragtime
members.description: Syncopated piano style made famous by Scott Joplin.

members.title: Zydeco
members.description: Accordion and washboard dance music of Louisiana Creoles.

members.title: Techno
members.description: Machine-driven dance music first made by the Belleville Three.

members.title: Doo-wop
members.description: Street-corner vocal harmony style with nonsense-syllable backing.

members.title: House music
members.description: Four-on-the-floor dance music from 1980s Chicago clubs.

intruders.title: Trip hop
intruders.description: Slow, moody breakbeat style associated with Massive Attack and Portishead.
intruders.why: It emerged in Bristol, England, though its name and beats borrow from hip hop.

intruders.title: Grime
intruders.description: Rapid-fire MCing over sparse 140 bpm electronic beats.
intruders.why: It originated in East London in the early 2000s; it resembles rap but grew from UK garage.

intruders.title: Drum and bass
intruders.description: Fast breakbeats with heavy sub-bass lines, grown from jungle.
intruders.why: It developed in the UK rave scene of the 1990s.

theme: Active mainly in the Baroque era (roughly 1600 to 1750).
decoy: Major composers of the 17th and 18th centuries

members.title: Johann Sebastian Bach
members.description: Leipzig church musician behind the Brandenburg Concertos and the Mass in B minor.

members.title: George Frideric Handel
members.description: German-born composer who settled in London and wrote the Water Music.

members.title: Antonio Vivaldi
members.description: Venetian priest who taught at an orphanage and wrote The Four Seasons.

members.title: Georg Philipp Telemann
members.description: Hamburg music director with thousands of works to his name.

members.title: Henry Purcell
members.description: English composer of Dido and Aeneas and royal ceremonial odes.

members.title: Arcangelo Corelli
members.description: Rome-based violinist whose concerti grossi set a model across Europe.

members.title: Jean-Philippe Rameau
members.description: French composer and theorist who wrote a treatise on harmony.

members.title: Johann Pachelbel
members.description: Nuremberg organist best known for a canon over a repeating bass.

members.title: Francois Couperin
members.description: French keyboard composer who wrote a treatise on harpsichord playing.

intruders.title: Joseph Haydn
intruders.description: Austrian who spent decades as music director for the Esterhazy princes.
intruders.why: A Classical-era composer, active mainly after 1750 and central to the symphony and string quartet.

intruders.title: Christoph Willibald Gluck
intruders.description: German-born opera composer who worked in Vienna and Paris.
intruders.why: His reform operas from the 1760s onward belong to the early Classical period.

intruders.title: Luigi Boccherini
intruders.description: Italian cellist-composer who spent most of his career in Madrid.
intruders.why: Born in 1743, he is a Classical-era composer of quintets and symphonies.

theme: LPs by The Beatles.
decoy: Landmark British and American pop-rock LPs of the 1960s

members.title: Rubber Soul
members.description: 1965 LP whose cover photo shows the band's faces stretched and distorted.

members.title: Revolver
members.description: 1966 LP with a line-drawing and photo-collage cover by Klaus Voormann.

members.title: Abbey Road
members.description: 1969 LP whose cover shows four men walking over a zebra crossing.

members.title: Let It Be
members.description: 1970 LP from filmed sessions, with final production by Phil Spector.

members.title: Help!
members.description: 1965 LP serving as soundtrack to a comedy adventure film.

members.title: Please Please Me
members.description: 1963 LP, most of it recorded in a single day at EMI's studios.

members.title: Yellow Submarine
members.description: 1969 LP with one side given over to George Martin's orchestral film score.

members.title: A Hard Day's Night
members.description: 1964 soundtrack LP full of ringing twelve-string Rickenbacker guitar.

members.title: Magical Mystery Tour
members.description: 1967 US LP pairing a TV-film soundtrack with recent stand-alone singles.

intruders.title: Pet Sounds
intruders.description: 1966 LP with bicycle bells and barking dogs, its cover photo taken at a zoo.
intruders.why: A Beach Boys album, masterminded by Brian Wilson; it is often paired with Rubber Soul and Revolver as their rival.

intruders.title: Aftermath
intruders.description: 1966 LP with marimba and Appalachian dulcimer, written entirely by the group.
intruders.why: A Rolling Stones album, released the same year as Revolver and Pet Sounds.

theme: Traditional Japanese instruments: the Japanese forms themselves (even where descended from continental models), not their Chinese or Korean counterparts.
decoy: Traditional East Asian instruments

members.title: Koto
members.description: Long zither with thirteen strings on movable bridges, plucked with finger picks.

members.title: Shakuhachi
members.description: End-blown bamboo flute with five finger holes, linked to Zen monks.

members.title: Taiko
members.description: Large barrel drums played with heavy sticks in energetic ensembles.

members.title: Biwa
members.description: Short-necked lute played with a large wedge-shaped plectrum to accompany narrative song.

members.title: Sho
members.description: Mouth organ of seventeen bamboo pipes used in gagaku court music.

members.title: Hichiriki
members.description: Short double-reed bamboo pipe with a piercing tone, used in gagaku.

members.title: Kokyu
members.description: Small bowed lute with three or four strings and a square body.

members.title: Shinobue
members.description: High-pitched transverse bamboo flute heard at festivals and in theatre.

members.title: Tsuzumi
members.description: Hourglass-shaped hand drum whose lacing the player squeezes to change its tone.

intruders.title: Guzheng
intruders.description: Long zither with about twenty-one strings on movable bridges, plucked with finger picks.
intruders.why: A Chinese zither; the koto descends from this family, so the two look nearly identical.

intruders.title: Gayageum
intruders.description: Twelve-string zither with movable bridges, traditionally strung with silk.
intruders.why: A Korean zither, closely resembling the koto.

theme: Dances in triple meter: three beats to the bar.
decoy: Historical and folk dances that became art-music forms

members.title: Waltz
members.description: Turning couple dance that swept the ballrooms of 19th-century Vienna.

members.title: Mazurka
members.description: Polish folk dance with shifting accents, stylized by Chopin in dozens of pieces.

members.title: Polonaise
members.description: Stately Polish processional dance that opened court balls.

members.title: Sarabande
members.description: Slow, dignified dance movement at the heart of the Baroque suite.

members.title: Landler
members.description: Austrian country couple dance with hopping and stamping steps.

members.title: Galliard
members.description: Energetic Renaissance dance full of leaps, usually played after a slower partner.

members.title: Courante
members.description: Running dance that usually comes second in a Baroque suite.

members.title: Chaconne
members.description: Set of variations over a repeating bass, like Bach's for solo violin.

members.title: Jota
members.description: Lively folk dance of Aragon with quick leaping steps.

members.title: Minuet
members.description: Elegant French court dance, a standard inner movement of Classical symphonies.

intruders.title: Gavotte
intruders.description: French court dance beginning halfway through the bar, found in Baroque suites.
intruders.why: It is in duple time (4/4 or 2/2), despite sitting beside minuets and sarabandes in Baroque suites.

intruders.title: Allemande
intruders.description: Moderate German-derived dance that opens many Baroque suites.
intruders.why: It is in 4/4 time, though it is the standard partner of the courante.

intruders.title: Pavane
intruders.description: Slow processional Renaissance dance, usually followed by a livelier partner.
intruders.why: It is in duple time; its customary partner, the galliard, is the one in triple time.

theme: Compositions by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky.
decoy: Famous 19th- and early 20th-century Russian orchestral and stage works

members.title: Swan Lake
members.description: 1877 ballet about a princess turned into a bird by a sorcerer.

members.title: The Nutcracker
members.description: 1892 Christmas ballet featuring the Sugar Plum Fairy and a celesta solo.

members.title: The Sleeping Beauty
members.description: 1890 ballet after Perrault's fairy tale, premiered at the Mariinsky Theatre.

members.title: 1812 Overture
members.description: Concert overture scored for cannon fire and pealing church bells.

members.title: Marche Slave
members.description: 1876 orchestral march on Serbian folk tunes, written for a war-relief concert.

members.title: Capriccio Italien
members.description: 1880 orchestral fantasy on tunes heard during a carnival season in Rome.

members.title: The Queen of Spades
members.description: 1890 opera after Pushkin about a gambler obsessed with a secret of three cards.

members.title: Manfred Symphony
members.description: 1885 program symphony after Byron's dramatic poem.

members.title: Pathetique Symphony
members.description: Final symphony, premiered in St Petersburg in 1893 and ending with a slow movement.

members.title: Iolanta
members.description: 1892 one-act opera about a blind princess in Provence.

intruders.title: Scheherazade
intruders.description: 1888 orchestral suite on tales from the Arabian Nights, with a solo violin narrator.
intruders.why: By Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov, a contemporary Russian composer of the same era.

intruders.title: Pictures at an Exhibition
intruders.description: 1874 suite of musical portraits of artworks, famous in Ravel's orchestration.
intruders.why: By Modest Mussorgsky; the popular orchestral version is Ravel's.

intruders.title: The Firebird
intruders.description: 1910 ballet for the Ballets Russes after a Russian folk tale.
intruders.why: By Igor Stravinsky; a Russian fairy-tale ballet like those in the set.

theme: Stage musicals with music composed by Andrew Lloyd Webber.
decoy: Blockbuster West End musicals of the 1970s to 1990s

members.title: Cats
members.description: 1981 show adapted from T. S. Eliot's book of poems about felines.

members.title: Evita
members.description: 1978 show about Eva Peron, with lyrics by Tim Rice.

members.title: Jesus Christ Superstar
members.description: Rock opera first released in 1970 as a double album, with lyrics by Tim Rice.

members.title: Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat
members.description: Biblical show that began in 1968 as a short piece for a school concert.

members.title: Sunset Boulevard
members.description: 1993 show adapted from Billy Wilder's film about a faded silent-screen star.

members.title: Starlight Express
members.description: 1984 show about a train race, with the whole cast on roller skates.

members.title: Aspects of Love
members.description: 1989 romantic show adapted from a David Garnett novella.

members.title: Whistle Down the Wind
members.description: 1996 show adapted from the story of children who hide a fugitive in a barn.

members.title: The Phantom of the Opera
members.description: 1986 show after Gaston Leroux's novel, set beneath the Paris Opera house.

intruders.title: Les Miserables
intruders.description: Show adapted from Victor Hugo's novel, opening in London in 1985.
intruders.why: Music by Claude-Michel Schonberg; it shares producer Cameron Mackintosh with several of the set.

intruders.title: Miss Saigon
intruders.description: 1989 show relocating Madama Butterfly's story to the Vietnam War.
intruders.why: Music by Claude-Michel Schonberg, produced by Cameron Mackintosh at Drury Lane.

intruders.title: Blood Brothers
intruders.description: 1983 Liverpool-set show about twins separated at birth.
intruders.why: Book, music and lyrics are by Willy Russell; it ran in the West End alongside Lloyd Webber's hits for decades.

theme: Free-reed instruments: each note comes from a reed that swings freely back and forth in a close-fitting slot.
decoy: Reed-driven wind instruments outside the orchestra

members.title: Harmonica
members.description: Pocket-sized mouth instrument with a row of holes, played by blowing and drawing.

members.title: Accordion
members.description: Bellows-driven instrument with a piano-style or button keyboard for the right hand.

members.title: Concertina
members.description: Small hexagonal bellows instrument with buttons at each end.

members.title: Melodica
members.description: Keyboard instrument blown through a mouthpiece or flexible tube.

members.title: Sheng
members.description: Chinese mouth organ of bamboo pipes set in a round wind chest.

members.title: Harmonium
members.description: Pump organ supplied by foot pedals or a hand-worked bellows.

members.title: Bandoneon
members.description: Square button-box bellows instrument at the heart of Argentine tango.

members.title: Khaen
members.description: Lao mouth organ of long bamboo pipes bound in two rows.

members.title: Hulusi
members.description: Chinese gourd wind instrument with a melody pipe and drone pipes.

intruders.title: Bagpipes
intruders.description: Bag-fed instrument with a fingered melody pipe and drone pipes.
intruders.why: Its chanter and drones use beating cane reeds that close against the pipe, not free reeds, though it is wind-fed like an accordion.

intruders.title: Pipe organ
intruders.description: Keyboard instrument with ranks of pipes supplied from a wind chest.
intruders.why: Most of its pipes are flue pipes, and its reed stops normally use beating reeds; the harmonium only imitates it.

theme: Instruments fitted with frets.
decoy: Lutes and other necked string instruments from around the world

members.title: Lute
members.description: Pear-shaped Renaissance instrument with a pegbox bent back at a sharp angle.

members.title: Banjo
members.description: Round drum-like body with a skin head, often with a short fifth string.

members.title: Viola da gamba
members.description: Six-string bowed instrument held between the legs, popular before the cello.

members.title: Balalaika
members.description: Russian instrument with a triangular body and three strings.

members.title: Bouzouki
members.description: Greek long-necked instrument with a rounded back and paired strings.

members.title: Appalachian dulcimer
members.description: Elongated box laid across the lap and strummed over a raised fingerboard.

members.title: Charango
members.description: Small Andean ten-string instrument, traditionally with an armadillo-shell back.

members.title: Pipa
members.description: Chinese pear-shaped instrument held upright and played with fingerpicks.

members.title: Ukulele
members.description: Hawaiian four-string instrument developed from Portuguese imports.

members.title: Cittern
members.description: Renaissance wire-strung instrument with a flat back and a small body.

intruders.title: Oud
intruders.description: Short-necked pear-shaped instrument of the Arab world, played with a long plectrum.
intruders.why: Its fingerboard is fretless; it is the direct ancestor of the European lute, which did have frets.

intruders.title: Shamisen
intruders.description: Japanese three-string instrument with a square skin-covered body, played with a large plectrum.
intruders.why: Its long neck is fretless, though its skin-headed body makes it resemble a banjo.

theme: Musical devices first built in the 20th century (1901 or later).
decoy: Instruments that rely on novel mechanisms or electricity

members.title: Theremin
members.description: Played without touch by moving the hands near two antennas.

members.title: Ondes Martenot
members.description: French keyboard instrument also played by sliding a ring along a wire.

members.title: Hammond organ
members.description: Organ with spinning tonewheels and drawbars, often paired with a rotating speaker.

members.title: Mellotron
members.description: Keyboard that plays back a strip of recorded tape for each key.

members.title: Chapman Stick
members.description: Long fretboard with ten or twelve strings, tapped with both hands.

members.title: Trautonium
members.description: German instrument played by pressing a wire down onto a metal rail.

members.title: Minimoog
members.description: Compact portable synthesizer with an integrated keyboard and pitch wheel.

members.title: Electric guitar
members.description: Guitar whose magnetic pickups feed a signal to an amplifier.

members.title: Roland TR-808
members.description: Programmable drum machine famous for its booming bass drum sound.

intruders.title: Sousaphone
intruders.description: Wrap-around bass horn with a forward-facing bell, built for marching bands.
intruders.why: Developed in the 1890s at John Philip Sousa's request; it is strongly associated with 20th-century jazz and marching bands.

intruders.title: Player piano
intruders.description: Piano that plays itself by reading a perforated paper roll.
intruders.why: Roll-operated self-playing pianos such as the Pianola were already built in the 1890s; their heyday came in the early 20th century.

theme: Each act's first studio album.
decoy: Landmark rock and rap albums acclaimed as classics

members.title: Are You Experienced
members.description: 1967 album by a power trio led by a Seattle-born guitarist.

members.title: The Velvet Underground & Nico
members.description: 1967 album with an Andy Warhol banana on the cover.

members.title: Horses
members.description: 1975 album produced by John Cale, with a Robert Mapplethorpe cover photo.

members.title: Illmatic
members.description: 1994 Queensbridge rap album with beats from DJ Premier and Pete Rock.

members.title: Boy
members.description: 1980 album by a Dublin quartet, produced by Steve Lillywhite.

members.title: Definitely Maybe
members.description: 1994 album by a Manchester band, released on Creation Records.

members.title: Is This It
members.description: 2001 New York garage-rock album produced by Gordon Raphael.

members.title: The Stone Roses
members.description: 1989 Manchester album with a lemon-strewn, Pollock-style painted cover.

members.title: Ten
members.description: 1991 Seattle album named after a basketball player's jersey number.

members.title: Appetite for Destruction
members.description: 1987 Los Angeles hard-rock album released on Geffen Records.

intruders.title: Nevermind
intruders.description: 1991 Seattle-scene album produced by Butch Vig for DGC Records.
intruders.why: Nirvana's second album; their first was Bleach (1989). Its breakthrough success makes it feel like an arrival.

intruders.title: London Calling
intruders.description: 1979 London double album whose cover shows a bass guitar being smashed onstage.
intruders.why: The Clash's third album, after The Clash (1977) and Give 'Em Enough Rope (1978).

theme: Classical works whose home key is a minor key.
decoy: Cornerstones of the symphony and concerto repertoire

members.title: Beethoven's Fifth Symphony
members.description: 1808 symphony built from a terse four-note opening motif.

members.title: Mozart's Symphony No. 40
members.description: 1788 symphony, one of three he wrote in a single summer.

members.title: New World Symphony
members.description: Dvorak's 1893 symphony, written during his stay in America.

members.title: Rachmaninoff's Piano Concerto No. 2
members.description: 1901 concerto opening with tolling piano chords, dedicated to his doctor.

members.title: Grieg's Piano Concerto
members.description: 1868 concerto opening with a timpani roll and a cascading piano flourish.

members.title: Mendelssohn's Violin Concerto
members.description: Concerto premiered in Leipzig in 1845, the soloist entering almost at once.

members.title: Dvorak's Cello Concerto
members.description: 1895 concerto begun in New York, a pillar of the cello repertoire.

members.title: Sibelius's Violin Concerto
members.description: His only concerto, first heard in 1904 and revised a year later.

members.title: Brahms's First Symphony
members.description: 1876 symphony whose finale theme recalls Beethoven's Ninth.

intruders.title: Tchaikovsky's Violin Concerto
intruders.description: 1878 concerto written at Lake Geneva, once dismissed as unplayable.
intruders.why: It is in D major, though it sits in the same Romantic concerto canon as Mendelssohn's and Sibelius's.

intruders.title: Beethoven's Violin Concerto
intruders.description: 1806 concerto that begins with four soft timpani strokes.
intruders.why: It is in D major, unlike his Fifth Symphony.

intruders.title: Brahms's Violin Concerto
intruders.description: 1878 concerto written for his friend, the violinist Joseph Joachim.
intruders.why: It is in D major, unlike his First Symphony.

theme: Acts that recorded for Motown Records or its in-house labels (Tamla, Gordy, Soul) in the 1960s.
decoy: Classic 1960s American soul and R&B acts

members.title: The Supremes
members.description: Detroit trio fronted by Diana Ross, famous for sequined gowns.

members.title: The Temptations
members.description: Detroit vocal group known for sharp choreography and five-part harmony.

members.title: Marvin Gaye
members.description: Washington-born singer behind the 1971 concept album What's Going On.

members.title: Stevie Wonder
members.description: Blind multi-instrumentalist who signed as an eleven-year-old prodigy.

members.title: Four Tops
members.description: Detroit quartet with Levi Stubbs's urgent baritone lead.

members.title: Smokey Robinson & the Miracles
members.description: Vocal group led by a high-voiced singer and prolific songwriter.

members.title: Martha and the Vandellas
members.description: Detroit girl group fronted by Martha Reeves.

members.title: The Jackson 5
members.description: Brothers from Gary, Indiana, fronted by the youngest of them.

members.title: The Marvelettes
members.description: Girl group from Inkster, Michigan, whose 1961 hit was about a mail carrier.

members.title: Gladys Knight & the Pips
members.description: Atlanta family vocal group with the lead singer's brother among the backing.

intruders.title: Aretha Franklin
intruders.description: Detroit-raised singer, daughter of a famous Baptist preacher.
intruders.why: She recorded for Columbia and then Atlantic in the 1960s, never Motown, despite growing up in Detroit.

intruders.title: Otis Redding
intruders.description: Georgia soul singer with a raw, pleading delivery.
intruders.why: He recorded for Stax's Volt label in Memphis, Motown's main soul rival.

intruders.title: The Ronettes
intruders.description: New York girl group with towering hairdos and Wall of Sound productions.
intruders.why: They recorded for Phil Spector's Philles Records, not Motown, despite the girl-group sound.

theme: Fitted with sympathetic strings: extra strings, normally left unbowed and unstopped, that ring in response to the played ones.
decoy: Classical and folk string instruments of South Asia and Europe

members.title: Sitar
members.description: Long-necked Indian instrument with a gourd body and curved metal frets.

members.title: Sarod
members.description: Fretless Indian instrument with a metal fingerboard and a skin-covered belly.

members.title: Sarangi
members.description: Short bowed Indian instrument stopped with the cuticles of the fingers.

members.title: Hardanger fiddle
members.description: Norwegian folk fiddle decorated with mother-of-pearl inlay and ink drawings.

members.title: Viola d'amore
members.description: Baroque bowed instrument often topped with a carved head instead of a scroll.

members.title: Nyckelharpa
members.description: Swedish keyed fiddle whose wooden tangents stop the melody notes.

members.title: Baryton
members.description: Bowed viol-family instrument for which Haydn wrote over a hundred trios.

members.title: Esraj
members.description: Bowed Indian instrument with a fretted neck, common in Bengal.

members.title: Dilruba
members.description: North Indian bowed instrument associated with Sikh devotional music.

members.title: Rubab
members.description: Afghan short-necked lute carved from a single piece of mulberry wood.

intruders.title: Tanpura
intruders.description: Long-necked Indian lute that sustains a drone behind singers and soloists.
intruders.why: All of its four to six strings are plucked in turn; it has no sympathetic strings, though its buzzing bridge makes it shimmer like a sitar.

intruders.title: Saraswati veena
intruders.description: South Indian lute with a large wooden body and a gourd under the neck.
intruders.why: Its seven strings are four melody strings and three side drone strings, all plucked; it has no sympathetic strings.

theme: Transposing instruments: their standard parts are written at a different pitch from the one that sounds, including by whole octaves.
decoy: Orchestral, band, and jazz instruments with unusual notation conventions

members.title: Alto saxophone
members.description: Mid-sized curved single-reed instrument common in jazz and concert bands.

members.title: Tenor saxophone
members.description: Larger single-reed instrument with a crook bent like a pipe stem, central to jazz.

members.title: Flugelhorn
members.description: Valved brass instrument with a wide conical bore and a mellow tone.

members.title: Contrabassoon
members.description: Double-reed instrument of very deep range, its long tube folded several times.

members.title: Bass clarinet
members.description: Deep single-reed instrument with a curved metal neck and upturned bell.

members.title: Alto flute
members.description: Larger, lower flute with a curved or straight headjoint.

members.title: Guitar
members.description: Six-string fretted instrument usually tuned E-A-D-G-B-E.

members.title: Double bass
members.description: Largest bowed string instrument of the orchestra, played standing or perched on a stool.

members.title: Glockenspiel
members.description: Set of small steel bars in a keyboard layout, played with hard mallets.

members.title: Oboe d'amore
members.description: Baroque double-reed instrument with a pear-shaped bell, favored by Bach.

intruders.title: Viola
intruders.description: Four-string bowed instrument slightly larger than the violin, reading alto clef.
intruders.why: Its parts are written at sounding pitch; the unusual alto clef changes how notes are notated, not what pitch sounds.

intruders.title: Alto trombone
intruders.description: Small slide brass instrument that usually reads alto clef.
intruders.why: It is written at concert pitch, unlike the alto saxophone and alto flute.

intruders.title: Bass trombone
intruders.description: Slide brass instrument with extra valves for its lowest notes.
intruders.why: It is written at concert pitch in bass clef, even in British brass bands where the other brass parts are transposed.

theme: Classical works whose famous nickname was coined by someone other than the composer.
decoy: Famous classical works best known by a descriptive nickname

members.title: Moonlight Sonata
members.description: Beethoven piano sonata of 1801 opening with a slow, rippling triplet movement.

members.title: Emperor Concerto
members.description: Beethoven's fifth and last piano concerto, completed in 1809.

members.title: Jupiter Symphony
members.description: Mozart's last symphony, closing with a finale that combines five themes.

members.title: Minute Waltz
members.description: Chopin's brisk waltz in D-flat major, Op. 64 No. 1.

members.title: Raindrop Prelude
members.description: Chopin prelude with a note repeated almost throughout, finished in Majorca.

members.title: Revolutionary Etude
members.description: Chopin study of 1831 with torrential left-hand runs.

members.title: Unfinished Symphony
members.description: Schubert's two-movement symphony in B minor from 1822.

members.title: Farewell Symphony
members.description: Haydn symphony whose finale has the players leave one by one.

members.title: Clock Symphony
members.description: Haydn symphony whose slow movement has a steady ticking accompaniment.

intruders.title: Eroica Symphony
intruders.description: Beethoven's third symphony, first planned as a tribute to Napoleon.
intruders.why: Beethoven himself titled it 'Sinfonia eroica' on the 1806 first edition.

intruders.title: Pastoral Symphony
intruders.description: Beethoven's sixth symphony, with birdcalls and a thunderstorm.
intruders.why: Beethoven named it 'Pastoral-Sinfonie' himself and gave its movements descriptive headings.

intruders.title: Symphonie fantastique
intruders.description: Berlioz's 1830 program symphony built around a recurring melody.
intruders.why: Berlioz chose the title and wrote the program himself.

theme: Musical terms whose names are diminutives in their source language, literally meaning 'little X'.
decoy: Music words borrowed from Italian, French, and Spanish

members.title: Cornet
members.description: Valved brass instrument, shorter and more compact than a trumpet.

members.title: Ocarina
members.description: Egg-shaped vessel flute with finger holes, often made of ceramic.

members.title: Flageolet
members.description: Duct flute with thumb holes, popular in 17th-century France and England.

members.title: Castanets
members.description: Pair of shell-shaped wooden clappers held in the hand, heard in flamenco.

members.title: Tambourine
members.description: Shallow hand-held frame drum ringed with metal jingles.

members.title: Operetta
members.description: Light theatrical genre with spoken dialogue, perfected by Offenbach and Strauss.

members.title: Libretto
members.description: Text of an opera or oratorio, often printed separately for the audience.

members.title: Falsetto
members.description: Voice register above the normal range, produced with thinned vocal folds.

members.title: Motet
members.description: Polyphonic choral composition, usually sacred, often with a Latin text.

members.title: Ballet
members.description: Theatrical dance set to music, codified at the French royal court.

intruders.title: Trombone
intruders.description: Brass instrument whose pitch changes by extending a telescoping slide.
intruders.why: Its name is an Italian augmentative of tromba, meaning 'big trumpet', the opposite of a diminutive.

intruders.title: Vibrato
intruders.description: Slight regular wavering of pitch used by singers and string players.
intruders.why: An Italian past participle meaning 'vibrated'; its -ato ending only resembles diminutive endings like -etto.

intruders.title: Soprano
intruders.description: Highest standard singing voice, typical of leading heroines in opera.
intruders.why: From Italian sopra, 'above', with an adjective ending; it names a high part, not a small thing.

theme: Scales and modes whose third degree is flattened, lying three semitones above the tonic.
decoy: Named modes and scales used in Western, folk, and jazz music

members.title: Aeolian
members.description: Church mode played on the white keys from A up to A.

members.title: Dorian
members.description: Church mode played on the white keys from D up to D.

members.title: Phrygian
members.description: Church mode played on the white keys from E up to E.

members.title: Locrian
members.description: Church mode played on the white keys from B up to B.

members.title: Ukrainian Dorian
members.description: Dorian variant with a raised fourth step, heard in klezmer and Ukrainian folk music.

members.title: Harmonic minor
members.description: Seven-note pattern with an augmented second between its sixth and seventh steps.

members.title: Melodic minor
members.description: Pattern whose sixth and seventh steps are raised going up and lowered coming down.

members.title: Hungarian minor
members.description: Seven-note pattern with two augmented seconds: harmonic minor with a raised fourth.

intruders.title: Mixolydian
intruders.description: Church mode played on the white keys from G up to G.
intruders.why: Its third is major (G to B); only its lowered seventh gives it the bluesy, dark colour that makes it seem to fit.

intruders.title: Lydian
intruders.description: Church mode played on the white keys from F up to F.
intruders.why: Its third is major (F to A), like the major scale's, even though it looks like any other church mode.

intruders.title: Phrygian dominant
intruders.description: Fifth mode of harmonic minor, common in flamenco and klezmer music.
intruders.why: Its third is major, although it is named after Phrygian and derived from the harmonic minor.

theme: Chordophones: the sound comes from vibrating strings, however the player sets them going.
decoy: Keyboard and percussion-style instruments played with hammers, keys, or beaters

members.title: Piano
members.description: Keyboard instrument with felt hammers, dampers, and a sustain pedal.

members.title: Harpsichord
members.description: Baroque keyboard instrument, often built with two manuals and a buff stop.

members.title: Clavichord
members.description: Quiet domestic keyboard whose brass tangents allow a gentle vibrato.

members.title: Cimbalom
members.description: Hungarian concert instrument on legs, played with cotton-tipped beaters.

members.title: Hammered dulcimer
members.description: Trapezoidal box played with small hand-held hammers in folk music.

members.title: Berimbau
members.description: Brazilian bow with a gourd resonator, struck with a stick in capoeira.

members.title: Clavinet
members.description: Hohner electric keyboard with a percussive, funky tone.

members.title: Santoor
members.description: Persian and Kashmiri trapezoid played with light walnut mallets.

members.title: Virginal
members.description: Small rectangular keyboard instrument popular in Tudor England.

intruders.title: Toy piano
intruders.description: Miniature keyboard instrument whose hammers strike small metal rods.
intruders.why: It has no strings: the hammers hit metal rods, so it is an idiophone despite looking like a small piano.

intruders.title: Celesta
intruders.description: Keyboard instrument whose felt hammers strike steel plates over wooden resonators.
intruders.why: Its sound comes from struck steel plates, not strings, though it looks and plays like an upright piano.

intruders.title: Kalimba
intruders.description: Thumb piano with metal tines mounted on a wooden board or box.
intruders.why: Its sound comes from plucked metal tongues (lamellae), not strings, despite the 'piano' nickname.

theme: Songs whose best-known hit version is a cover: another artist had released the song first.
decoy: Signature hits of major singers and bands

members.title: Hound Dog
members.description: Elvis Presley's 1956 rock-and-roll hit, written by Leiber and Stoller.

members.title: I Will Always Love You
members.description: Whitney Houston's 1992 soundtrack ballad with an unaccompanied opening.

members.title: Respect
members.description: Aretha Franklin's 1967 Atlantic soul single, recorded in New York.

members.title: Nothing Compares 2 U
members.description: Sinead O'Connor's 1990 ballad, written by Prince, with a close-up video.

members.title: Tainted Love
members.description: Soft Cell's 1981 synth-pop hit, written by Ed Cobb.

members.title: All Along the Watchtower
members.description: The Jimi Hendrix Experience's 1968 hit with layered guitar solos.

members.title: Twist and Shout
members.description: The Beatles' 1963 album closer, recorded in a single take.

members.title: I Love Rock 'n' Roll
members.description: Joan Jett and the Blackhearts' 1981 hard-rocking single.

members.title: Mr. Tambourine Man
members.description: The Byrds' 1965 folk-rock hit with jangling twelve-string guitar.

intruders.title: Manic Monday
intruders.description: The Bangles' 1986 hit, written by Prince under a pseudonym.
intruders.why: The Bangles' single was the song's first release; Prince's own demo stayed unreleased for decades.

intruders.title: Crazy
intruders.description: Patsy Cline's 1961 country hit, written by Willie Nelson.
intruders.why: Cline's single was the first released recording; Nelson's own version came out afterwards.

theme: Works left incomplete when their composer died and brought to performable form by someone else.
decoy: Major works usually heard in versions edited or orchestrated by a second hand

members.title: Mozart's Requiem
members.description: Latin Mass setting commissioned anonymously through an intermediary in 1791.

members.title: Turandot
members.description: Puccini opera about an icy Chinese princess and her three riddles.

members.title: Mahler's Tenth Symphony
members.description: Symphony whose opening Adagio is often performed on its own.

members.title: Prince Igor
members.description: Borodin opera about a 12th-century prince, featuring the Polovtsian Dances.

members.title: Bartok's Viola Concerto
members.description: Concerto commissioned in 1945 by the violist William Primrose.

members.title: Elgar's Third Symphony
members.description: Symphony commissioned by the BBC and first performed in 1998.

members.title: Lulu
members.description: Berg's twelve-tone opera drawn from two plays by Frank Wedekind.

members.title: Khovanshchina
members.description: Mussorgsky opera about princely intrigue and the Old Believers in 1680s Russia.

members.title: The Tales of Hoffmann
members.description: Offenbach's fantastical opera in which a poet recounts three loves.

intruders.title: Carmen
intruders.description: Bizet opera about a Seville cigarette-factory worker and a soldier.
intruders.why: Bizet finished it and saw its 1875 premiere; Guiraud's sung recitatives, added after Bizet's death, replaced spoken dialogue in a work that was already complete.

intruders.title: Boris Godunov
intruders.description: Mussorgsky opera about a tsar's troubled reign, drawn from Pushkin.
intruders.why: Mussorgsky completed two versions himself and it premiered in 1874; Rimsky-Korsakov's famous edition is a revision, not a completion.

theme: Digital sound encodings that keep every sample intact: none applies lossy, perceptual data reduction.
decoy: Digital audio formats and codecs from the CD era onward

members.title: ADAT
members.description: Alesis eight-track digital tape format of 1991, recorded on S-VHS cassettes.

members.title: ALAC
members.description: Apple's audio codec, released as open source in 2011.

members.title: Monkey's Audio
members.description: Windows-born audio codec that saves files with the .ape extension.

members.title: Audio CD
members.description: Red Book disc storing 16-bit, 44.1 kHz stereo audio.

members.title: DVD-Audio
members.description: Disc format launched in 2000, offering up to 24-bit, 192 kHz stereo.

members.title: Super Audio CD
members.description: Sony and Philips disc carrying one-bit DSD audio.

members.title: Dolby TrueHD
members.description: Blu-ray surround audio format built on Meridian's MLP technology.

members.title: DTS-HD Master Audio
members.description: Blu-ray surround audio format with a backward-compatible core stream.

members.title: Shorten
members.description: 1990s audio codec once popular for trading live concert recordings.

intruders.title: Digital Compact Cassette
intruders.description: Philips's 1992 digital tape format whose decks also played ordinary cassettes.
intruders.why: It uses PASC, a lossy perceptual codec related to MPEG-1 Audio Layer I.

intruders.title: Dolby Digital
intruders.description: Surround audio format for DVDs and cinemas, also known as AC-3.
intruders.why: It is a lossy perceptual codec, unlike its Blu-ray sibling Dolby TrueHD.
